high_co2.default: My head is pounding. The air feels thick. We need to open the vents, even if the ash gets in.
high_co2.paranoid: The air is poison. Thick. My skull is a vice. We crack the vents or we choke — ash or no ash.
high_co2.cautious: My head is pounding. The air feels thick. We need to open the vents, even if the ash gets in.
high_co2.realist: CO₂ is climbing — headache, heavy air. Crack a vent or the filter is finished. Ash comes with it.
high_co2.reckless: Head's fuzzy. Air's garbage. Crack the vents. We'll deal with the ash when it lands.
high_co2.denialist: Just a stuffy room. Open a vent if you want. I am fine. The filter will sort it.
high_co2.fatalist: Air goes bad. Head pounds. Vents or no vents, the ash finds us either way.

has_seen_radiation.default: I felt the dose climb. We log it and we scrub.
has_seen_radiation.paranoid: The dosimeter twitched. Or I imagined it. Either way I will not take my coat off indoors.
has_seen_radiation.cautious: I felt the dose climb. Not much — enough. We log it, we scrub, we do not pretend it is nothing.
has_seen_radiation.realist: Radiation is on us now. Small number, real number. Keep the suits sealed when we go out.
has_seen_radiation.reckless: Got a tick on the counter. Still standing. Wash the boots and keep moving.
has_seen_radiation.denialist: The needle moved. Instruments lie. I feel fine.
has_seen_radiation.fatalist: The dose goes up. It always does. Write it down so the next one knows.

has_experienced_storm.default: Storm hit. Seal what we can and wait it out.
has_experienced_storm.paranoid: The sky is eating the world. Fallout on the roof. Do not open anything. Not the hatch. Not a crack.
has_experienced_storm.cautious: Storm hit. Ash and worse. Seal the intake if we can. No trips until it breaks.
has_experienced_storm.realist: Fallout storm. Outdoor exposure spikes. Stay under concrete until the wind dies.
has_experienced_storm.reckless: Ugly sky. Storm. If someone has to go out, make it short and make them count.
has_experienced_storm.denialist: Weather's loud. It will pass. Always does.
has_experienced_storm.fatalist: Storm again. The ash settles on everything. We wait. That is the work.

filter_failing.default: Filter health is low. We need a spare before the air turns.
filter_failing.paranoid: The filter is dying. I can taste dust. If it fails we breathe the outside — and the outside wants us dead.
filter_failing.cautious: Filter health is low. Spare cartridges, or we start sharing headaches with the ash.
filter_failing.realist: Air filter is wearing out. Scrap and a swap, or indoor air turns against us.
filter_failing.reckless: Filter's shot soon. Swap it when we can. Or don't. Throat's already rough.
filter_failing.denialist: Filter light is yellow. Yellow is fine. Yellow is not red.
filter_failing.fatalist: Filter fails eventually. Everything does. Still — write it before the air does.

freezing_shelter.default: Indoor cold is biting. Fuel the heater before sleep.
freezing_shelter.paranoid: Cold is in the walls. Heater dead or starving. We freeze careful or we freeze stupid.
freezing_shelter.cautious: Indoor cold is biting. Fuel the heater. Stack bodies if we must. Do not sleep wet.
freezing_shelter.realist: Bunker temperature is below safe. Heater fuel or we lose fingers and morale with them.
freezing_shelter.reckless: Cold as a grave. Fire up the heater or burn something. I'm not sitting still for this.
freezing_shelter.denialist: A bit chilly. Put on another layer. The heater can wait.
freezing_shelter.fatalist: Cold comes in. We write it. We feed the stove if there is fuel. If not, we endure.

history_continuity_reclamation_decree.default: Garrison command changed. Old permits void; re-issue at Checkpoint Gamma.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.paranoid: Voss's bulletin is gone. Harven's is up, and it says nothing about why. That is a coup that signs its own name.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.cautious: Command changed hands overnight. All orders void, permits re-issued. We get new papers before we move anywhere.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.realist: Garrison command changed. Old permits void; re-issue at Checkpoint Gamma. Standard succession, fast execution.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.reckless: New colonel, same checkpoints. Papers, no papers — we go where we need to go.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.denialist: New name on the bulletin. Command changes hands. Nothing about our shelter changes.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.fatalist: Harven signs, Voss does not. Whoever signs, the checkpoints stay. We queue either way.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.empath: Someone lost command of something they built. The board is repapered and nobody says goodbye.
history_continuity_reclamation_decree.sociopath: Harven replacing Voss means new permits, new bribe rates, new friction. We adjust fees accordingly.

history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.default: The rate card predates the Exchange by six years. Nobody has revised a single line of it.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.paranoid: The rate card is older than the Exchange — a drought surcharge from a company called Halloway. The apocalypse changed nothing. They were always deciding who paid more.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.cautious: The card predates the war. A pre-Exchange contractor's sheet, unrevised. Worth remembering when we negotiate.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.realist: Six-year-old surcharge sheet, still enforced. The price of water was decided before the water was poisoned.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.reckless: An old company's old sheet still sets our water price. Somebody should revise it with a crowbar.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.denialist: A piece of paper from before. Rates are rates. We pay what everyone pays.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.fatalist: The card was old before the bombs. It will be old after. We drink on their terms or not at all.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.empath: Odalen explains the queue the way someone explains a family arrangement — tired, patient, four thousand times.
history_hydro_baron_rate_card_origin.sociopath: Old pricing sheet from before the exchange. A monopoly pricing baseline we can exploit when bartering.

history_deserter_coalition_founding.default: Someone has scratched a tally into the transformer housing — one mark per person who made it here and stayed.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.paranoid: A tally scratched into the transformer housing — one mark per person who stayed. The first mark is dated to an embargo that 'never happened.' It happened.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.cautious: The substation holds a marked count of people who refuse to return to garrison. We count them carefully — they are not the garrison's friends.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.realist: Deserters have been filtering to this substation since the fuel embargo. The tally is honest about who stays.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.reckless: A tally of people who walked off. Good for them. Someone should keep count of the ones who were right.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.denialist: Scratches on a wall. Could be anyone. People exaggerate numbers in the dark.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.fatalist: Marks on a wall, one per deserter. The wall fills or the wall doesn't. We all end up counted somewhere.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.empath: Each mark is someone who made it here and stayed. The first one dates to a thing that never officially happened.
history_deserter_coalition_founding.sociopath: Tally on the housing gives an exact headcount of unaligned deserters. Useful inventory of manpower.

history_cold_count_before_the_lab.default: Four researchers signed up for a civil-defence isotope survey and never left. The lab outlived the agency that commissioned it.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.paranoid: Four researchers signed up for an isotope survey and never left. Their instruments were bought, not salvaged. The lab outlived the agency that ordered it — ask why nobody came back.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.cautious: The lab predates the Exchange. Four staff, bought instruments, a survey mandate. We log what they tell us and verify it ourselves.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.realist: The Cold Count predates the war: four surveyors who stayed at their post. Their instruments outlasted their agency.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.reckless: Four scientists, one lab, bought gear, no exit plan. Either the smartest or the most stubborn people in the sector.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.denialist: A survey team that kept working. People do that. It does not mean the sky is falling — it already fell, and we are fine.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.fatalist: Four people measured what was coming and stayed to watch it arrive. That is either purpose or refusal. Either way, they wrote it down.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.empath: They must have known. They bought instruments instead of tickets out.
history_cold_count_before_the_lab.sociopath: Four researchers stuck at their post with intact calibration gear. High value salvage or technical assets.

history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.default: The homestead's log predates the Allocation Schedule by three winters of stocked supply runs.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.paranoid: The homestead was resupplied every winter for a decade before the Exchange — by nobody the sector can identify. Someone knew. Someone is still supplying it. Find out who.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.cautious: The log shows years of stocked runs before the Allocation Schedule existed. The Provisioned knew before anyone. We watch what they do with that.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.realist: The homestead's stock runs predate the war. The Provisioned spent a decade preparing alone and never told anyone.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.reckless: They saw it coming and stocked for it, and never warned a soul. Either brilliant or as selfish as they come — probably both.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.denialist: A well-stocked shelter. Lucky people. It does not mean they knew anything special.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.fatalist: Somebody prepared for ten years and it still was not enough to stop the Exchange. Prepare or not, the ash does not read logs.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.empath: Someone believed this was coming with enough certainty to spend a decade on it — and never once sold that certainty to anyone who could have used it.
history_the_provisioned_advance_knowledg.sociopath: Decade of secret stocking confirmed. Locate the supply cache coordinates; their inventory belongs to whoever claims it.

history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.default: A conscript at Checkpoint Gamma: Voss was shot by his own staff for refusing a direct order to fire on a grain convoy.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.paranoid: There it is. Voss refused to fire on a grain convoy and his own staff shot him for it. The boy confessed it over drinks. They killed their commander for a grain convoy — what will they do to us.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.cautious: A conscript says Voss was killed by his own men for refusing an order. Unverifiable, unretractable now that it is written. We treat it as an open question.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.realist: Account one of three: the conscript's. Voss refused a firing order and was shot by his own staff. One witness, at a checkpoint, drunk.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.reckless: They shot their own colonel for not shooting civilians. Whatever else that is, it is a story worth repeating.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.denialist: A drunk boy's story about his officers. Soldiers talk. Most of it is barracks noise.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.fatalist: However Voss died, he is dead, and the conscript will not sleep better for telling us. Neither will we.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.empath: He said it like a confession, then asked me not to repeat it. I cannot promise him that — it is already in this journal.
history_checkpoint_conscripts_confession.sociopath: Source at the checkpoint, low value, volunteered after alcohol. Claims a commander was shot by his own staff over a convoy order. Unverified. Keep the source warm; he will talk again.

history_quartermasters_paperwork.default: The quartermaster: Voss requested reassignment to the coastal evacuation liaison post at the outset of Phase V. Nobody has heard from him since.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.paranoid: The quartermaster is too calm. 'Reassignment, coastal liaison.' Nobody has heard from Voss since. Paperwork that tidy is paperwork built to bury something.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.cautious: Account two: Voss requested reassignment to the coast at the start of Phase V. Paperwork is real; whereabouts unknown. We keep both accounts.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.realist: The quartermaster's record: Voss rotated to a coastal liaison post, Day 240. Plausible, ordinary, and impossible to check from here.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.reckless: Officers leave the worst postings all the time. Maybe he did. Maybe the paperwork says so because the paperwork was told to.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.denialist: There — a reassignment order. He left for the coast like any officer. The other story is a drunk kid's imagination.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.fatalist: Rotate out, rotate in; the garrison grinds on either way. Wherever Voss is, the paper will not say more than it says.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.empath: The quartermaster finds it entirely unremarkable. That is the most remarkable thing about it.
history_quartermasters_paperwork.sociopath: Contact at the motor pool: reassignment order, coastal liaison, Day 240. Paperwork in order. Useful only as evidence of how well the garrison files things it does not want read.

history_the_intercepted_cipher.default: An unregistered, low-power signal using an authentication cipher retired with Voss's old command. Ruhl: 'I don't chase ghosts. I log them.'
history_the_intercepted_cipher.paranoid: A cipher retired with Voss's command, transmitted three weeks after Day 240, logged and never forwarded. It is him, or someone with his keys. Either way someone is alive out there using a dead man's code.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.cautious: Account three: an unregistered burst using a retired cipher, logged by signals, never forwarded. Ruhl's assessment is the most honest thing in the file.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.realist: The intercept: low-power, unregistered, cipher retired with Voss's command. Could be him; could be a code never properly decommissioned.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.reckless: A ghost is broadcasting on a dead cipher. Ruhl says she logs ghosts, not chases them. Somebody ought to chase this one.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.denialist: A radio signal on an old code. Equipment quirks. Static in, static out. It does not mean anything.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.fatalist: Whoever it is, on a dead cipher, they will answer when they want to be answered. Logged or not, it changes nothing we can do.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.empath: Whoever is out there still signs with a dead commander's code. That is either respect or a very old habit.
history_the_intercepted_cipher.sociopath: Intercept, low power, cipher retired with the old command. Ruhl logs it; I log that Ruhl logs it. If it is him, he owes us. If it is not him, someone useful is alive.

history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.default: Three pages, one code, marked PAID in three different hands. Nobody currently employed by any of the three ledgers can say who opened the account.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.paranoid: One code, three ledgers, marked PAID in three hands — and nobody can say who opened the account. The oldest page is signed with one initial. They are hiding something and they have been for years.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.cautious: A debt code appears in three independent ledgers, always PAID, never identifiable. We note it and do not touch it.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.realist: The ledger nobody signed: three matching pages, one code, three different hands, all PAID, account untraceable. The ink on the oldest is the best-preserved thing in the cache.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.reckless: Somebody paid something for years and nobody claims it. The Tally does not know, Iversen does not know, the cache does not know. I want to know.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.denialist: Old paperwork, old debts, old ink. It was settled before any of this mattered. Close the file.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.fatalist: A debt without a debtor is still a debt. It will surface when it wants to surface. These pages have outlived everyone who could explain them.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.empath: Someone kept records this long — through a war, through a change of command — of a debt nobody claims. That is a life's worth of care about something.
history_the_ledger_nobody_signed.sociopath: Three verified PAID debt vouchers with unidentified account origins. Leverage on whichever ledger house holds the duplicate.

faction_military_history.default: Unit records and regimental archives reveal the pre-Exchange command structure that preceded the Garrison. The photographs are formal and the captions are terse. An institution shows itself in how it lined people up.
faction_military_history.paranoid: Old war photos. Officers staring through us. The Garrison still operates on their unrevoked directives.
faction_military_history.cautious: Pre-war military documentation. It shows how the regional chain of command disintegrated into martial law.
faction_military_history.realist: Archival unit photographs and regimental notes: supply lines, command posts, insignia, all documented before the detonations. The records stop abruptly that morning. What survives is enough to put a few names to faces.
faction_military_history.reckless: Old brass in sepia. They had rifles, orders, and no clue what was dropping from the sky.
faction_military_history.denialist: Just old service photos. Standard garrison history before everything went sideways.
faction_military_history.fatalist: Regiments named on paper that do not exist anymore. Their ghosts still hold the bunker.

faction_state_propaganda.default: Civil defense leaflets and wartime state posters show the curated optimism broadcast before the Exchange. The reassurances were already stale when printed, if the supply queues were any measure. Keep the paper and distrust the promises.
faction_state_propaganda.paranoid: Paper lies glued to concrete. The state told everyone to shelter and then sealed the gates from the inside.
faction_state_propaganda.cautious: Wartime propaganda broadsheet. Promising orderly relocation and civil defense reserves that never arrived.
faction_state_propaganda.realist: State morale print: cheerful figures, firm type, instructions to remain calm. The same press run promised railway service that had already been diverted for ordnance. It is a record of what they wanted believed.
faction_state_propaganda.reckless: Bright colors, bold letters, complete fiction. Good kindling if nothing else.
faction_state_propaganda.denialist: Official notices from the ministry. Standard civil order protocols for emergency conditions.
faction_state_propaganda.fatalist: Smiling workers on glossy paper. They starved in the same basements as the rest of us.

faction_military_operations.default: Tactical log fragments detail the final troop redeployments toward the perimeter bunkers. The handwriting degrades page by page. The last entries are numbers only.
faction_military_operations.paranoid: Operation orders for scorched-earth withdrawal. They burned their own fuel depots to starve the towns.
faction_military_operations.cautious: Operational dispatch logs. Outlines perimeter sweep sectors and fallback zones during the initial strikes.
faction_military_operations.realist: Unit log entries tracking munitions expenditure and vehicle attrition across the first week. The accounting stays professional long after the situation stops being manageable. It reads like a ledger outliving its office.
faction_military_operations.reckless: Tactical notes from officers who realized too late that reinforcements were not coming.
faction_military_operations.denialist: Routine patrol logs. Standard exercises during the alert phase.
faction_military_operations.fatalist: Hour by hour logs of radio silence falling over every sector until only static remained.

faction_military_deployment.default: Official deployment orders dispatching regional defense battalions to subterranean holdfast sectors. The movement tables are precise to the hour. Precision was not the problem.
faction_military_deployment.paranoid: Orders signed in carbon copy: seize civilian grain elevators and shoot any councilman who objects.
faction_military_deployment.cautious: Formal deployment manifests. Useful for identifying which bunkers were equipped with heavy armories.
faction_military_deployment.realist: Signed deployment documents detailing battalion assignments, ammunition allotments, and bunker coordinates. The paperwork is complete, and the plan it describes failed anyway. The coordinates alone justify keeping it.
faction_military_deployment.reckless: Old deployment orders. Useful roadmap for finding where they stashed the ordnance.
faction_military_deployment.denialist: Standard military transfers. All by the book, even when the book was burning.
faction_military_deployment.fatalist: Orders sending young men to guard empty crossroads while the sky tore open.

faction_civil_defense.default: Civil defense credentials and district sector notices reveal the emergency administration network. The wardens were issued whistles, rosters, and keys to the shelters. The keys mattered more than anything else that autumn.
faction_civil_defense.paranoid: Civil defense badges. The wardens who had keys to the community shelters while neighbors banged on iron.
faction_civil_defense.cautious: Warden documentation. Details fallout shelter air circulation specs and ration stockpiling protocols.
faction_civil_defense.realist: An emergency warden registry recording which municipal sectors received filtration equipment before the war. The distribution was uneven, and the registry notes it without comment. The omission is informative.
faction_civil_defense.reckless: Enamel badges from men who blew whistles at sirens. Did not stop a single megaton.
faction_civil_defense.denialist: Municipal emergency management tokens. Proves civil authorities had an orderly plan in place.
faction_civil_defense.fatalist: Badges for volunteers who stayed above ground to guide others into holes they could not enter.

faction_military_units.default: Insignia patches identify the specific armored and infantry regiments stationed across the valley. Collectors once traded these at market stalls. Identification matters more than sentiment does now.
faction_military_units.paranoid: Regimental crests of the units that turned their machine guns inward to secure their own rations.
faction_military_units.cautious: Unit patches recovered from the wasteland. Correlates vehicle wrecks with their parent armories.
faction_military_units.realist: Unit insignia tying the valley wrecks and abandoned posts to their parent regiments: an armored detachment, a border guard company. Lineage, in the end, is bookkeeping that outlives the book. The stitching survives the soldiers.
faction_military_units.reckless: Embroidered skull and eagle patches. Looks impressive on a coat, means nothing to fallout.
faction_military_units.denialist: Standard brigade insignia. Just uniform decoration from regular armed service.
faction_military_units.fatalist: Thread and cloth identifying divisions whose bones are powdered across the ruins.

faction_trade_guilds.default: Trade guild tokens and merchant charters record the commercial syndicates operating across the river routes. Their marks promised fair weight. The charters also record what happened when the weight was short.
faction_trade_guilds.paranoid: Guild marks of the merchant cartels. They monopolized salt and clean water within six months of the war.
faction_trade_guilds.cautious: Pre-war and early post-war trade charters. Clarifies barter ratios and safe route markers used by caravans.
faction_trade_guilds.realist: Guild insignia and route charters establishing the early trade consortiums between the valley settlements. Barter ratios and safe-passage marks are all written down. Those routes still decide who trades with whom.
faction_trade_guilds.reckless: Merchant badges. Those traders were ruthless, but their route maps are worth every coin.
faction_trade_guilds.denialist: Commercial guild tokens. Business continuity agreements to keep trade flowing.
faction_trade_guilds.fatalist: Coins and emblems of syndicates that traded gold for bread until the bread ran out too.

journal_casualty_records.default: A typed casualty list from the first strike waves, recording civilian and military losses by bunker zone. The columns stay neat long after the numbers stop being bearable. Someone did the bookkeeping anyway.
journal_casualty_records.paranoid: Names typed on cheap paper. Thousands marked deceased while their commanders sat in air-conditioned vaults.
journal_casualty_records.cautious: Verified casualty ledgers from Sector 4. A grim reference for tracing survivors and lost family lines.
journal_casualty_records.realist: A strike casualty manifest: name, service number, evacuation code, zone of loss. The counts stop being statistics once you have read enough of the names. I copy the spellings carefully in case anyone ever asks.
journal_casualty_records.reckless: Pages and pages of names. The world ended and someone still bothered to type the ledger.
journal_casualty_records.denialist: Preliminary missing-persons reports. Many of them probably made it to southern evacuation centers.
journal_casualty_records.fatalist: Neat rows of typewriter ink recording the end of four thousand lives on a Tuesday morning.

journal_soldier_letters.default: Unsent letters from garrison soldiers to families cut off on the surface as the fallout closed in. Most stop mid-thought, as if the writer expected to finish them later. None of them are finished.
journal_soldier_letters.paranoid: Private notes smuggled past the censors. They knew the rations were toxic weeks before they were relieved.
journal_soldier_letters.cautious: Soldiers personal correspondence. Gives human context and emotional weight to the concrete ruins.
journal_soldier_letters.realist: Handwritten letters out of the garrison: morale thinning, water rumored unsafe, hunger counted in days. The writers exaggerate and understate by turns, which is how you can tell it is honest. Not one was ever posted.
journal_soldier_letters.reckless: Love letters and regrets written on ration box cardboard. Stashes and secrets hidden between the lines.
journal_soldier_letters.denialist: Ordinary mail that was held up by communication disruptions. They will read them eventually.
journal_soldier_letters.fatalist: Words written to people who had already turned to ash when the pen touched the paper.

journal_religious_texts.default: Annotated liturgical texts and scriptures preserved in wasteland shelters, marked with prayers for the dead. The margins hold more handwriting than the printed pages. People needed somewhere to put the names.
journal_religious_texts.paranoid: Apocalyptic verses highlighted in red pen. People convinced themselves the fire was divine judgment.
journal_religious_texts.cautious: Religious texts recovered from the cloister. Shows how spiritual communities adapted to subterranean life.
journal_religious_texts.realist: A shelter scripture volume with funeral dates handwritten in the margins and counsel copied out for the sick. Whatever the theology, the book did steady work down here. The ribbon marker has moved many times.
journal_religious_texts.reckless: Holy book with pages missing for rolling paper. Still has the old hymns inside.
journal_religious_texts.denialist: Traditional faith texts. Good to keep old cultural traditions intact while we rebuild.
journal_religious_texts.fatalist: Prayers asking for mercy from an empty sky that answered with burning dust.

journal_exchange_day.default: Newspaper edition rushed to press on the morning of the Exchange, headline frozen in the first hours of the war. The inside pages are ordinary: weather, markets, a school fundraiser. The ordinary pages are the hardest to read now.
journal_exchange_day.paranoid: The morning edition of the end. Government denials on page one, while sirens were already sounding outside.
journal_exchange_day.cautious: Exchange Day newspaper preserved in a sealed mail pouch. Details the timeline of initial missile detections.
journal_exchange_day.realist: A special morning bulletin: launch detections, blackout orders, instructions to remain indoors. The typesetting is no different from any other Tuesday. That is the detail worth recording.
journal_exchange_day.reckless: Headline screaming nuclear war in eighty-point type. The ultimate historical souvenir.
journal_exchange_day.denialist: Temporary crisis reporting. Urging citizens to remain calm until negotiations resumed.
journal_exchange_day.fatalist: The last words ever printed on a press in this city. Wet ink that survived everyone who read it.
